docs.title: Glymph
docs.text:
Ambient RNA removal for single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq that measures the background instead of inferring it.

Quickstart The benchmark Slides Code on GitHub

19×faster per library than CellBender, on the same GPU 27 of 32libraries with truth where Glymph is more accurate per cell 3platforms: 10x Chromium, BD Rhapsody, Parse Evercode 0counts added: the output is whole numbers, never above the raw count

docs.title: The idea in one paragraph
docs.text:
Every droplet, well or split-pool barcode carries RNA its cell did not make. Existing deep-learning removers infer how much from a likelihood and priors, and the likelihood cannot pin that amount down. Glymph measures it. A gene that a cell type does not express is a silent gene there: it should read zero, so every count it shows is background. Each library contains thousands of these internal negative controls. Glymph reads the background off them, per library and per cell, holds it fixed, and lets a small autoencoder separate expression from background.

Measured, not inferred

The amount of background comes from silent genes, checked against genotype truth in mouse kidney.

Fast

A median of 98 s per library on one GPU, against 35 min for CellBender. 160,000 cells in 14 min.

Three platforms

Droplets, microwells and split-pool barcoding, with no vendor cell calls needed.

Whole counts

Integers in, integers out. No entry is ever higher than it was.

Per-cell error of the estimated background fraction, one point per library with truth. Points under the dashed line are libraries where Glymph is more accurate.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/swaruplab/glymph.git
cd glymph
pip install -e .
glymph run --input raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5 --output sample.h5ad

Glymph needs PyTorch and runs on one CUDA GPU; it also runs on CPU. See the quickstart.

TAKE-HOMEMeasure the background. Do not infer it.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: A small autoencoder, calibrated by measurement

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
Step What happens 1. Read The whole matrix: cells and empty partitions 2. Priors Empty level, cell threshold and ambient profile from the depth distribution; a plateau mode for droplets, a knee mode where there is no plateau 3. Train The autoencoder with its count mixture 4. Measure Cluster the embedding, find silent genes, measure the three amounts and a multiplier per cell 5. Refit Train again briefly with the amounts fixed and silent genes excluded from expression 6. Thin Remove whole counts, gene by gene, from the entries where background is most probable

Step 4 is the new part. Everything runs on one GPU, with the library held there as a sparse matrix.

docs.title: The model
docs.text:
A variational autoencoder built from fully connected layers. The encoder maps a barcode's counts to a low-dimensional embedding; the decoder turns the embedding into the cell's own expression profile. The expected counts are

  • the cell's own profile, from the decoder,
  • plus the ambient profile of its unit, times the measured amount,
  • plus the average cell profile of its pool, times the swapped fraction,

with a multinomial likelihood over the genes that have counts. The model is small on purpose: the difficulty is the amount of background, not the capacity of the network.

docs.title: The output rule
docs.text: For every gene, the number of counts to remove is the expected background of that gene summed over cells. They are taken from the entries where background is most probable. A false-positive budget (0.4% by default) lets a gene give up a little more than expected, and is the one dial that trades removal against counts kept. The result is an integer matrix in which no entry exceeds the raw count.

docs.title: Three platforms
docs.text:
Platform structure enters as two labels per barcode.

Platform Unit (shares ambient RNA) Pool (amplified together) Priors from 10x Chromium the library the library the plateau of empty droplets BD Rhapsody the cartridge the cartridge the knee of the depth distribution Parse Evercode the first-round well the sublibrary the knee, per sublibrary

Without vendor cell calls, Glymph's cell count on a BD Rhapsody spleen library is 8,061; the vendor pipeline calls 8,061.

TAKE-HOMEA small model is enough once the amount of background is no longer its job.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
54 libraries, three platforms, six tools, measured truth

54libraries 3platforms 6tools, same GPU model 12mixtures never used in development

Every tool ran on every library, and every score comes from a truth that does not depend on any tool:

  • 27 human and mouse mixtures (cell lines on 10x, BD Rhapsody and Parse, a nuclei mixture, six xenografts). Every count of the other species is background.
  • 5 mouse kidney libraries pooled from three strains, where genotypes give the background of every cell (Janssen et al. 2023).
  • 8 Parse libraries with one tissue per well, and 14 libraries without truth, scored on count integrity and marker leakage.

Glymph 0.3.1 is at its default false-positive budget (0.4%), CellBender 0.3.2 at its default (1%). Genes that collect reads aligned to the wrong genome, such as ribosomal RNA on mouse Gm42418, are masked for every tool by a rule that uses raw counts only.

docs.title: Speed
docs.text:
Wall time per library on one A30 GPU (SoupX and DecontX on four CPU cores). Bars are medians over 54 libraries.

Glymph's median is 98 s per library and CellBender's 35 min. The whole benchmark took Glymph 2.0 GPU-hours and CellBender 35.2.

One 20,000-cell library copied one to eight times, on one A30 with 24 GB. Time and memory only, never accuracy.

At 160,000 cells Glymph takes 14 min with 48 GB of memory; CellBender takes 4 h 29 min with 112 GB.

docs.text:
One point per library with truth. Lower is better; points under the dashed line are libraries where Glymph is more accurate.

Glymph has the lower per-cell error on 27 of 32 libraries with truth and the higher rank agreement on 28.

docs.title: Where Glymph does not win yet
docs.text:
• Clean tissue. On the four xenograft libraries never used in development Glymph removes 79% of cross-species counts against 65%, but it also removes 2.0 times the expected same-species background and keeps 97.3% of the cells' own counts against 99.3%.
  • BD Rhapsody removal. 91.6% against 93.0% on the mixture never used in development, with a quarter of CellBender's per-cell error.
  • Repeat runs. Libraries with very little background give few silent genes to test, and their result moves by up to 8 points of removal between runs.
  • Marker genes on Parse tissue. Glymph keeps 93.7% of cluster-specific marker counts in their own cluster on the Parse libraries, against 99.5% for CellBender: a sign of the same over-cleaning.

The full tables, one row per library and tool, are in the repository under runs/20261117-0607_glymph-031-alltier/.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Very clean libraries. With little background, only a handful of genes can be tested as silent, and the measured level can come out too high. On xenograft skin Glymph removes about 2 times the expected same-species background.
  • Run-to-run variation on such libraries: up to 8 points of cross-species removal between two runs of the same code.
  • A single homogeneous population has no silent genes. Glymph then keeps the empty-partition level and its learned swapped fraction.
  • It needs the empty partitions. A matrix of called cells only cannot be run.
  • Doublets. A doublet of two cell types is held to the silent genes of its main type, which strips the partner's exclusive genes. Such cells are flagged (glymph_doublet_like); drop them before calling doublets, or run with --spare-doublets.

docs.title: Does it need cell type labels or marker lists?
docs.text: No. Clusters come from the model's own embedding.

docs.title: Does it change counts upward?
docs.text: Never. The output is the input minus whole counts.

docs.title: Which budget should I use?
docs.text: The default (0.4%). A larger --fpr removes more and keeps fewer of the cells' own counts; the benchmark page shows the trade-off.

docs.title: How was it tested?
docs.text: On 54 libraries from three platforms against CellBender, scAR, SoupX and DecontX, with species, genotype and tissue truth. Twelve libraries were never used in development. See the benchmark.

docs.title: What is the licence?
docs.text: MIT. See LICENSE in the repository.

docs.title: Why "Glymph"?
docs.text: After the glymphatic system, which clears waste from the brain.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text: The gap, and what Glymph does about it

docs.title: Every count has three possible sources
docs.text: A count in the matrix can come from the cell in the partition, from free RNA in the suspension that every partition captures (ambient RNA), or from a molecule that changed barcode during amplification (swapped reads). Only the first is biology. Background is not a rare artifact: published estimates are 3 to 35% of a cell's counts in mouse kidney, with medians of 17% and 35% in nuclei from frozen tissue (Janssen et al. 2023, Genome Biology).

docs.title: What was missing
docs.text:
Speed

The standard tool trains a new model on every library. In our benchmark its median was 35 min per library on one A30 GPU, and 4 h 29 min for 160,000 cells.

A measured amount

A flexible model can explain background as expression and fit the data just as well, so priors decide the amount. CellBender removed 74% of the expected same-species background across 27 mixtures.

More than one platform

One plateau of empty droplets and one ambient profile per run is a 10x premise. BD Rhapsody and Parse Evercode fall outside it.

Intact counts

The faster alternatives return fractional counts or, in one case, counts higher than the raw data.

docs.title: Silent genes are built-in negative controls
docs.text:
A gene that a cell type does not express should read zero in those cells. Whatever it does read is background. This is the same logic as reads of another species in a mixture, or of another genotype in a pooled sample, but it needs no special experiment.

Glymph clusters the cells on the model's own embedding, finds for every cluster the genes whose counts are no more than background alone explains, and uses the counts on those genes as the measurement. No labels and no marker lists are involved.

docs.title: Three amounts, each read off the data
docs.text:
Amount What it is Ambient, per partition A constant amount, in units of what an empty partition holds Ambient, with depth Ambient RNA that grows with the depth of the cell; nuclei carry it Swapped reads Proportional to depth, with the average profile of the pool

In mouse kidney nuclei pooled from three strains, genotypes give the true background of every nucleus: a constant of 0.55 empty-partition levels plus 0.47 per unit of depth. Glymph measured 0.56 to 0.59 plus 0.47 to 0.54 from silent genes alone.

docs.title: Then every cell gets its own amount
docs.text:
Background is not one number per library. Each cell's own counts on its cluster's silent genes say whether it carries more or less than the trend, and it gets its own multiplier, shrunk toward the trend when its evidence is thin. The same silent genes constrain the model: it may not explain counts on them as expression.

TAKE-HOMEEvery library carries thousands of negative controls. Glymph reads the background off them.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/swaruplab/glymph.git
cd glymph
pip install -e .

Requirements: Python 3.10 or newer, PyTorch 2.2 or newer, numpy, scipy, pandas, h5py, anndata. One CUDA GPU is recommended; a typical library takes one to four minutes there. Glymph also runs on CPU.

docs.title: Run one library
docs.text:
glymph run --input raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5 --output sample.h5ad --plot sample.rank.png

The input must be the raw matrix with every barcode, not the filtered one: Glymph needs the empty partitions.

Inputs it reads: 10x .h5, MEX folders (Cell Ranger, STARsolo, BD Rhapsody), BD Rhapsody tables, Parse split-pipe folders, and .h5ad.

docs.title: Run many libraries on several GPUs
docs.text:
glymph batch --manifest libs.tsv --outdir out --devices cuda:0,cuda:1,cuda:2,cuda:3

One library per GPU at a time.

docs.title: Platform structure
docs.text:
For split-pool data, pass an .h5ad whose obs says which barcodes share ambient RNA and which were amplified together:

glymph run --input parse_sublibrary.h5ad --output clean.h5ad --unit-key unit --pool-key pool

docs.title: What comes out
docs.text: Where What X cleaned integer counts for called cells layers["raw"] the input counts obs["glymph_background_fraction"] the share of each cell's counts removed obs["glymph_cell_probability"] probability that the barcode holds a cell obs["glymph_doublet_like"] cells that clearly express their cluster's silent genes obsm["X_glymph"] the embedding sample.report.json timings, thresholds, the measured amounts and their diagnostics

docs.title: Options worth knowing
docs.text: Option Default Meaning --fpr 0.004 False-positive budget: trades removal against counts kept --spare-doublets off Do not hold doublet-like cells to their cluster's silent genes --no-silent-broad Use only genes abundant enough to test one by one --calib-seeds 3 Clusterings tried for the measurement; the middle estimate is kept --device auto cuda:0, cpu, ...
